flags.item: The six-hourly refresh failed for 24 hours because receipts for delisted fixtures were counted as rejected [verified 2026-10-24 against the failing run's own log and the green run after the fix]
flags.detail: Hotspawn's fixtures API only returns cards with status=scheduled and drops a card once it kicks off, so a static external-odds receipt points at a fixture that is no longer listed within a day. tools/corroborate.py classified those as 'unmatched / rejected', and the publish gate 'external receipts validated against the dataset' fails whenever any receipt is rejected. Every scheduled refresh from 2026-10-23T17:13Z to 2026-10-24T16:19Z therefore failed at the gate (40 of 41 checks passing) and the published site stayed frozen at the 2026-10-23T17:13:12Z snapshot. Fixed in PR #62: such a receipt is now classified as historical evidence, kept and dated on the coverage page, excluded from every price and from the gate, which still fails on malformed receipts and on receipts that name the wrong teams for a fixture we do list. The first green run after the fix is 40110996859 (2026-10-24T16:19Z, 241/241 fixtures, 41/41 gates, 16 historical receipts).
flags.verification: verified 2026-10-24 against the failing run's own log and the green run after the fix

flags.item: Two market rows publish venue weights that do not sum to 1.0 (#1067878, #1079080) [re-derived 2026-10-24 with audit/session_5ff8e6bf/verify_published.py]
flags.detail: The per-venue 'weight' fields are published as collected (Pinnacle 0.36, Polymarket 0.24, Kalshi 0.18, Unibet 0.10 on #1067878, which sums to 0.88 because Bovada returned no price in that build; #1079080 is a single thin Polymarket venue published at 0.24). The published probability is the correctly normalised weighted mean of those quotes, so no probability is wrong: an independent re-derivation reproduces p0 for every market row within 0.01. The display is what is inconsistent, and a reader adding up the weights on the card would not get 100%. Fixture #1067878 has since left the Hotspawn list (the card kicked off or was removed); the statement is kept as a historical observation about that card.

flags.item: Pinnacle JSON receipts answer HTTP 401 to some datacenter clients and HTTP 200 in a browser [fetched 2026-10-24; 200 with straight-market JSON]
flags.detail: Every Pinnacle row links its receipt at guest.api.arcadia.pinnacle.com/0.1/matchups/<id>/markets/related/straight. A GitHub-runner harvest of all 241 source links recorded 401 for 8 of the 10 market-quote URLs, while the same URL fetched normally returns the straight-market JSON (spot-checked 2026-10-24 for matchup 1639121258: moneyline 155 / -184, cutoff 2026-10-24T17:00Z). The links are therefore valid for a human reviewer but not machine-resolvable from every host, so link-resolution counts taken from a cloud runner understate them.

flags.item: Pinnacle publishes each LoL series twice and the pick engine was using the (Kills) derivative [verified live 2026-10-23 (both matchup ids visible in one Pinnacle response)]
flags.detail: Pinnacle's guest API lists a series moneyline plus a parallel '(Kills)' market (e.g. 'Gen.G (Kills)' vs 'Invictus (Kills)'). In the 2026-10-23T11:42Z snapshot six of eight Worlds picks were taken from the (Kills) market: Gen.G vs Invictus Gaming carried 1.282/3.740 from matchup 1638758865 while the series market 1638748200 was 1.259/3.940. A kills derivative is not a series-winner price. Fixed in this build: tools/collect.py and tools/model.py now reject any participant name containing '(Kills)' or parentId derivatives, 8 derivative markets were excluded, and the 9 remaining market picks are all true series moneylines.
flags.verification: verified live 2026-10-23 (both matchup ids visible in one Pinnacle response)
